concepts.why: The patient's high body temperature and disseminated intravascular coagulation are consistent with severe heat stroke.

The patient's bilateral cerebellar hemisphere high-signal intensity on diffusion-weighted and FLAIR images and decreased perfusion in the right cerebellar hemisphere are consistent with heat-induced cerebellar injury.
The patient's laboratory results show disseminated intravascular coagulation.
The patient's laboratory results show hepatic dysfunction.
The patient's laboratory results show renal dysfunction.
The patient has a history of dementia.

The patient's bilateral cerebellar hemisphere high-signal intensity on diffusion-weighted and FLAIR images and decreased perfusion in the right cerebellar hemisphere are consistent with cerebellar dysfunction.
The patient's hepatic dysfunction, renal dysfunction, and disseminated intravascular coagulation are consistent with multi-organ failure.
It explains the low Glasgow Coma Scale score and the initial normal Head MRI and MRA findings that later showed cerebellar hemisphere high-signal intensity on diffusion-weighted and FLAIR images.

rationales.F01: Age is a risk factor for heat stroke and cerebellar injury, but not specific enough to rule in or out any concept.

rationales.F04: High body temperature is a hallmark of heat stroke and can cause multi-organ failure.

rationales.F10: Normal head MRI and MRA make cerebellar infarction less likely.
